newsitem.title: MEXICO: Pemex Q4, 1996 crude production, exports rise.
newsitem.headline: Pemex Q4, 1996 crude production, exports rise.

text.p: Mexican state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) on Tuesday said its crude output rose to 2.87 million barrels per day (bpd) in Q4, up from 2.404 million in the same quarter the previous year.
Over the year, its production averaged 2.858 million bpd, up from 2.617 million bpd in 1995. Exports in the fourth quarter increased to 1.556 million bpd, up from 1.211 million bpd in Q4 1995.

In a presentation of its 1996 results, Pemex also said natural gas production in the fourth quarter rose to 4.192 billion cubic feet per day (cfd) from 3.836 billion. Throughout 1996, it was 4.195 billion cfd compared with 3.759 billion in 1995.
It reported a 22 percent surge in net profits in 1996, rising to $1.933 billion from $1.583 billion. Pre-tax profits were $21.065 billion, a 32 percent rise from the year before.
Crude export revenues rose 43.1 percent to $10.705 billion in 1996, up from $7.48 billion in 1995.

During the year, the average production cost per barrel of crude rose slightly to $2.54 from $2.52 in 1995. The average price of its three brands of exported crude for the year was $18.94 per barrel, compared with $15.70 in 1995, Pemex said.
